read_only.applicability: HTTP console methods classified as mutating, including multipart send/upload. This is not the structural mob-events stale-cursor meaning of -32010; discriminate by method and data.

access_denied.applicability: Applicable ABAC action gates and access-administration checks. Additional denial context may be present. Some reads filter results instead of refusing the whole request; this is not an unconditional error on every method.

candidate_launch.applicability: A runtime-backed console of a candidate launch (runtime_options.mob_composition.authority = candidate) refuses, before anything is read or written, the methods that retire, respawn or reset a member, recompute the roster or rewire members (meta/retire, meta/retire_member, meta/respawn, meta/respawn_member, meta/reset, meta/reset_all, meta/delete_identity, meta/reconcile_identity and meta/topology/apply; meta/reconcile_edges answers a dry run flagged applied: false instead), meta/gating/decide, the console schedule writes (meta/schedule/create, update, pause, resume and delete), the ones that create a session (meta/ensure_member, meta/spawn_helper, meta/fork_helper, meta/fork_member and meta/attach_existing_session), the ones that admit member input or act on a member's runs (among them meta/console/send, including multipart, meta/console/voice/open, meta/console/recover_send, meta/run_flow, meta/reload_member, meta/stop_member_run and meta/force_cancel_member), the member declaration mutations (mob/adopt_member_identity_declaration and mob/apply_member_tool_declaration), and the operator mutations: the WorkGraph writes, meta/memory/quarantine/decide, the agent memory writes, the label sets and deletes, the access policy writes, meta/console/revoke_sessions, meta/blob/upload, meta/cancel_flow, the live channel verbs, a mobpack deploy with execute or a validation with rkat_validate, and a draft write (meta/mobpacks/create, save, delete, undo and redo) except to a store file the caller names outside the state directory and the gateway home that is not the store META_FLOW_EDITOR_DRAFT_STORE names. Reads still answer.

errors.note: -32602 with data.kind side_chat_restart_refused (operation respawn, agent_identity, source_member_id) refuses a console side chat, which is never respawned: its successor would be no fork of its source. Close it and fork the source again. meta/respawn_member, outside this contract, refuses it the same way.

-32602 with data.kind side_chat_restart_refused (operation reset, agent_identity, source_member_id) refuses a console side chat, which is never reset: its successor would be no fork of its source. Close it and fork the source again.

request.note: run_id is the member run's UUID from its run_started event (identity.run_id). A stale run_id is the typed not_current receipt, never an interrupt.

success.note: receipt is meerkat's WireRunStopReceipt, tagged by outcome: stopped { run_id, contributors }, not_current { run_id, current_run_id? } or not_stoppable { run_id, state }.

errors.note: Mob refusals (unknown member, unsupported member mode, host refusal) carry meerkat's typed code and structured data.

request.note: A side chat: a durable fork of the source's committed transcript end into a new member named agent_identity, with the source's role, profile and model overrides, runtime mode and tools, seated exempt from the mob definition's wiring rules so it is never wired to a peer whatever the source's role, and kept until it is retired, which needs agent.retire on the source. Gated on agent.spawn for agent_identity and on agent.view and agent.send for the source (-32030 naming the refused action); a source whose lineage already fills the access rules' walk (the source and seven ancestors) is refused -32030 with data.reason lineage_too_deep, for every caller, an admin included. A source the console's visibility policy hides is answered as unknown (-32001, data.kind identity_hidden_by_policy), as meta/fork_helper, outside this contract, answers it. A message_count (prefix) is refused. Offered in meta/capabilities where sessions persist, or where the composition did not record whether they do (the fork then refuses typed where they do not).

success.note: retention is until_closed. instructions lists each instruction the side chat inherited as history: state inherited (the source's revision activated in the side chat) or inactive with a reason (not_effective_in_source, body_unreadable, activation_refused); the side chat refuses its first turn naming an inactive key. The experience lists a side chat's sidebar row with side_chat_of, its source's identity; its console labels carry side_chat_of and side_chat_of_session (the forked source session), read from the durable fork record, and every agent check on a side chat is its source's: an allow must match the source or its lineage, and a rule that matches only the side chat grants nothing. A side chat is never respawned or reset (meta/respawn and meta/reset answer -32602 side_chat_restart_refused) and never adopted as an identity (mob/adopt_member_identity_declaration answers -32602 side_chat_adoption_refused).

errors.note: -32055 is a typed refusal: data.kind fork_source_unavailable (cause running, no_session for a seat that was never woken, which the fork does not wake, remote_read_unavailable or authority_unavailable), nothing forked; fork_source_changed (agent_identity, source_member_id), a side chat forked from another session of the source than the fork's checks read (a reset or a respawn ran in between); or unwired_seat_unavailable (wiring.rule seated_with_peers), a seated side chat with peer edges after all. For the last two the side chat is retired again and data.retired says whether that succeeded. -32001 is a source the console's visibility policy hides (identity_hidden_by_policy). Under a member auth binding a source whose session records another binding or none answers -32602 member_auth_binding_uncarried, nothing forked. -32037 is meerkat's fork_instruction_refused under the refuse policy. A committed fork whose seat failed keeps meerkat's fork_member_provision_failed data with its fork_session_id.

request.note: identity names the agent as meta/console/send names it (a public alias; a runtime member id the console knows is read as its identity). Gated on agent.view for the agent (-32030). Offered in meta/capabilities where the runtime's schedule host keeps console schedules; elsewhere the method answers -32601. Console-only: the stdin gateway does not dispatch the meta/schedule/* methods.

success.note: schedules lists the agent's console schedules, oldest first, each a console_schedule: schedule_id, identity, name (or null), content, trigger (the scheduler's trigger, tagged by type: once, interval or calendar), phase (active or paused), revision, sender (the principal the schedule sends as, null for an anonymous caller and when withheld), sender_hidden (true when the caller may view the agent but not send to it: only a caller who may send to the agent sees who its schedules send as), defined_at_utc, created_at_utc, updated_at_utc and next_due_at_utc (the next planned send of an active schedule, else null). The agent's own schedules (its schedule tools) and other schedules of the store are not listed, and the agent's schedule tools neither list nor change console schedules.

errors.note: -32601 where the gateway keeps no console schedules; -32602 for a missing or invalid identity; -32004 data.kind schedule_host_unavailable when the schedule store is unavailable; -32000 (data.error internal_error) when the console cannot read its agents or the store.

request.note: A deferred send of content (a non-empty string) to the agent identity names, at the trigger's times: the scheduler's trigger, tagged by type (once {due_at_utc}, interval {start_at_utc, every_seconds, end_at_utc?} or calendar {timezone, minute, hour, day_of_month, month, day_of_week, year?}, each calendar field {kind: any} or {kind: values, values}); an interval repeats at most once a minute (every_seconds of at least 60). Gated as meta/console/send is on this route, for the caller as the console resolves it, signed in or not: a writable console (-32010), a valid public alias, and agent.send for the agent under the live access policy (-32030). The schedule records that caller as its sender: the principal the console send would use, with the provider and issuer its token verified under (none for an anonymous caller), and the subject only for a verified signed-in human.

success.note: The schedule as meta/schedule/list answers it. Each due time is sent as a console send by the recorded sender, judged when it fires. The Console first admits the sender as it admits a live request by it: an anonymous sender only while the Console requires no sign-in; a principal only under the issuer the Console trusts then, past its provider policy and allowlist where sign-in is required, and past its session fence (Console sessions revoked after the schedule was defined refuse it, for every signed-in principal, a service identity included). Then it sends exactly as /console/send does once its caller is admitted: the candidate-launch refusal, a writable console, agent.send for the sender under the access policy then, an addressable agent whose input is not governed, and the identity-first send or the member lane. A refused or failed send fails that occurrence (delivery_failed) and the schedule keeps its later times; an agent the console no longer knows (a deleted identity, or a member without one that was retired) fails its sends the same way, and the schedule stays until it is deleted, while an identity released with meta/retire is materialized by the send, as by any console send. A send is deduplicated under its occurrence's delivery key in the sender's send scope, as a live send by the sender is, so a redelivered occurrence is sent once while the console's dedupe store holds the key (an in-memory store forgets it on restart); a send whose admission the Console could not observe (a timeout) is recorded failed although it may have been admitted. Sends carry origin console:schedule and the scheduler turn origin, through the Console router built last (its decisions and visibility); a fire on a gateway with no Console send path waits for one only in the first 30 seconds after the gateway's schedule host starts, and otherwise fails at once.

errors.note: -32001 data.kind unknown_identity when no agent of the console has the name; -32002 data.kind not_addressable for an agent that takes no console sends; -32004 data.kind governed_target for an agent whose input is governed (a governed send needs its Console human present, and a fire has none) or data.kind schedule_host_unavailable where no schedule firing host sends the gateway's schedules; -32602 for an invalid identity, a blank content, an interval under 60 seconds, or an invalid trigger (the scheduler's validation, an unknown time zone among them).

request.note: Changes the console schedule schedule_id of the agent identity names: its content, trigger or name, each kept when absent. Gated as meta/schedule/create. The update records the caller as the schedule's sender, whatever it changes, judges the agent again as a create does, and writes at the revision it read.

success.note: The changed schedule. Every update moves the schedule to a new revision and plans its next times again.

errors.note: -32001 data.kind schedule_not_found for a schedule that does not exist, was deleted, is no console schedule, or is another agent's. The other refusals are meta/schedule/create's. -32009 data.kind schedule_revision_conflict (expected_revision, actual_revision) when the schedule changed between this call's read and its write: nothing is changed, so the call never reverts that change.

request.note: Stops the console schedule's sends until it is resumed; pausing a paused schedule answers it as it is. Gated on a writable console and agent.send for the agent; the sender stays as it is.

errors.note: -32001 data.kind schedule_not_found for a schedule that does not exist, was deleted, is no console schedule, or is another agent's; -32602 for an invalid identity or schedule_id.

request.note: Resumes a paused console schedule. Gated as meta/schedule/create: the resume records the caller as the schedule's sender while it is still paused, at the revision it read, so no send goes out as the earlier sender and no change made meanwhile is put back, and judges the agent again as a create does.

errors.note: -32001 data.kind schedule_not_found for a schedule that does not exist, was deleted, is no console schedule, or is another agent's. -32602 for a schedule that is not paused.
